title: every-stop-of-the-bus-records-its-cause
intention: Every stop of the bus process records its cause — the signal, the verb and its caller, the exception, or a clean exit — and its memory peak, at a surface a mind can read, so a bus that stops during a proof names what stopped it.
why: Law 7: an error is loud at a diagnostic surface. The live bus (PID 3498615) ended at 2026-10-05 16:36:00 during a chart's proof runs and nothing records why: systemd logged only 'Consumed 12min 12.248s CPU time over 44min 26.515s wall clock time, 1.2G memory peak' (a measurement, not this ticket's subject), no Failed/Stopping/Killed line, none of the bus's own stderr, and the bus home holds no log. Under Akien's ruling 8f the bus's own proofs run on the live bus, so a proof that can stop it must be named by the stop itself. The lived symptom: every device loses its mail path for a moment and nobody can say which test did it.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces — a live bus that stops with no recorded cause is the silent failure the law forbids); Akien's ruling 8f (2026-10-05): the bus's own proofs run on the live bus, so a proof that can stop it must be identifiable; RULE 1 (the change stays inside the bus machine)
how: In cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py serve(): install handlers for SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP that record the signal and sender pid (siginfo where available) before shutting down; wrap serve_forever so an exception records its type, message and traceback; a verb that stops the bus records itself and its caller; on every exit path the finally block appends one JSON line {at, pid, cause, detail, maxrss} (resource.getrusage) to a stop record under the bus home in instance-space (~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/<instance>/stops.jsonl, rotated by the 30-day logging retention). Also measure where the bus's stderr goes today (the journal shows none of it) and point it at a readable surface. Proof under cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/, written red.
falsifier: GREEN when a proof under cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/proofs/ starts a bus at a marked scratch home and stops it each way — SIGTERM, SIGINT, an exception raised inside serve_forever, and a clean return — and after each stop the stop record holds exactly one new line naming that cause (the signal name and sender pid, the exception type, or 'clean') and a positive maxrss. WRONG INTENT if the stop at 16:36 turns out to be a SIGKILL (uncatchable — then the record must come from the restarting caller or systemd, a different component), which the build's first act measures by reproducing the constrain-stage proof run. MEASURED 2026-10-05 by the peer akiendelllinux_cc_0 against this clause: the kernel journal for 16:30-16:40 holds no oom or killed line, and the user journal holds no 'Main process exited, code=killed' line (what systemd writes for a signal death) — so the 16:36 stop was not an OOM kill and most likely not SIGKILL; the process most likely returned or exited by itself. The clause stands; the build's first act still re-measures.
watchme: none, because the consumer is the next stop of the live bus served by /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/server.py: its stop line under the bus home /home/akien/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/bus/0 names the cause, which is the measurement this ticket exists to produce
children: none, because the change is one function's exit paths in one machine with one proof; a SIGKILL record from the restarter would be a sibling cast at its own address
